The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=0$ the particle is located at the position $x=6.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=3?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=3$ is equal to its position at $t=0$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [0,3].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(3)=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{3}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(0)=6$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{0}^{3}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=0$ to $t=3.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}v(t)\,\text{d}t=5.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(3)=6+5=11
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=3$ is $x=11.$
